headline: Micron falls 3% in first regular session after record quarter
summary: Shares slid about 3% Thursday morning despite record $54.23B revenue and above-consensus guidance; the pullback is read as profit-taking after a 268% year-to-date run and some margin softness. JPMorgan's Harlan Sur called it 'a decisive beat-and-raise' and D.A. Davidson said the cycle may extend rather than peak. Western Digital fell 2%.

headline: Goldman lifts Micron target to $1,250 but stays Neutral; Mizuho target to $1,400, Deutsche target $1,550
summary: Goldman raised its target from $1,100 to $1,250, citing 26 long-term customer agreements covering ~35% of expected revenue through FY2030 but warning new industry supply could slow HBM pricing in 2028. Mizuho lifted its target to $1,400 from $1,300 (Outperform) on supply tightness into 2028; Deutsche kept Buy and its $1,550 target despite 'squishiness' on margins.

headline: 10-year Treasury hits 5.33%, highest since 2002, capping the Micron-led tech bid
summary: Stocks opened higher on Micron then faded as the 10-year touched 5.34%; S&P 500 -0.2%, Nasdaq -0.1%, Dow -0.4% around 10:30 ET with crude up 1.4%. ISM manufacturing came in at 54.5 vs 55.0 expected (prices paid 77.9 from 71.1), and Waller's 10:00 ET speech was about FRED data and AI, with no policy comment.

headline: Barclays sees at least $30B of hyperscaler revenue upside for Nvidia in 2026 and 2027
summary: Analyst Tom O'Malley used Nvidia's disclosed share of top-five cloud capex (44% estimate for 2027) to imply hyperscaler revenue above Barclays' base case by at least $30B in each year, and said sentiment can keep improving on buybacks and the Hugging Face deal. Separately Cantor reiterated Overweight with a $350 target.

headline: Google TPUs launched to orbit on SpaceX Transporter-18 for Project Suncatcher
summary: A pathfinder satellite carrying Google TPUs lifted off from Vandenberg Thursday to test radiation and heat handling for solar-powered AI compute in low Earth orbit. Google says orbit offers up to eight times more solar power than Earth; SpaceX plans Nvidia-chip AI satellites by late 2027.

headline: JPMorgan keeps Overweight on Alphabet after Gemini 4 Argon, says Google must reclaim AI leadership
summary: Shares rose as much as 1.5% premarket before fading. Argon launches at $2 per million input and $10 per million output tokens, initially only to trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind program; JPMorgan said Google needs to 're-establish itself at the frontier' and flagged strength in coding, agentic workflows and cybersecurity.

headline: Meta spells out Muse monetisation: a fee on savings, subscriptions, 200M small businesses
summary: President Dina Powell McCormick told CNBC Meta is 'thinking through the potential of taking a fee when we help you save money' and sees subscription opportunities, with roughly 200M small-business owners already on Meta's platforms. Muse is the top App Store download and Meta says it will come to its AI glasses in coming months.

headline: Deutsche Bank names Meta and ServiceNow among nine picks for the next leg of the AI trade
summary: Deutsche's strategists said the better opportunities now sit in targeted hardware value-chain names and software companies turning AI agents into revenue, citing Meta's investment at scale and its raised 2026 capex floor of $130B.

headline: TSMC weighs multi-fab Texas campus at $20B+ per fab, contingent on CHIPS credit renewal
summary: Bloomberg reports early-stage planning for a Texas campus separate from the $265B Arizona commitment, with each fab costing at least $20B; renewal of the 35% advanced-manufacturing tax credit before year-end could decide it. North American customers are over 75% of wafer revenue. TSMC: 'no comment on market rumors'. Shares rose 1.3% in Taipei Thursday as the Taiex gained 0.9%.

headline: BofA lists Marvell, Nvidia and Micron among five must-own chips for Q4, lifts AI data-centre forecast to $2.2T
summary: BofA raised its 2030 AI data-centre market forecast to $2.2T from $1.8T (40% annual growth) and named NVDA, INTC, MRVL, MU and LRCX, citing Marvell's Oct 6 analyst day and XPU ramp, Nvidia's buybacks and GTC events, and Micron's buybacks starting Dec 9. Q4/Q1 have historically delivered 300-500bp of outperformance for chips.

headline: ISM manufacturing 54.5 in September, prices paid jumps to 77.9; 10-year yield holds above 5.3%, highest since 2002
summary: The headline missed the 55.0 consensus but prices paid rose from 71.1 to 77.9 and new orders to 55.3, keeping the bond sell-off going. The 10-year traded as high as 5.34% Thursday after breaking its 2007 peak Wednesday; RKT, LDI and FIGR all opened lower.

headline: 30-year fixed mortgage rate 7.60% as of Sept 30, up 2bp, with the 10-year at a 20-year high
summary: Mortgage News Daily's latest reading is 7.60% after a day that started better on PCE and ended worse. Thursday's reading will not post until the afternoon, but with yields higher again after ISM it is unlikely to improve.

headline: Goldman adds Amazon to its US conviction list with a $375 twelve-month target
summary: Goldman cites AWS revenue of $42.2B in Q2, up 37% year on year and the fastest in 18 quarters, plus total revenue above $200B for the first time. The stock still slipped 0.9% at the open as yields rose.

headline: Amazon signs 20-year deal with Constellation for Calvert Cliffs nuclear output and funds a 190 MW uprate
summary: The agreement covers 690 MW from the Maryland plant, with Amazon financing roughly 190 MW of added capacity due 2030-2032. It is Amazon's first deal to fund an uprate at an existing reactor and supports Constellation's licence renewals.

headline: Sarandos at Bloomberg Screentime: Netflix is 'not growing as fast as I want'
summary: The co-CEO said growth has fallen short of his ambitions and pointed to live events (about 5% of a $20B content budget, 1% of viewing) and creator-led video as the levers. Shares were down 2.0% in the first hour ahead of the Oct 20 report.

headline: Guggenheim raises Netflix target to $80 from $75, keeps Buy
summary: Analyst Michael Morris held Q3 estimates at $12.9B revenue and said investor worries about revenue trajectory and the content slate are overdone. It follows Deutsche Bank's upgrade to Buy earlier in the week.

headline: BYD September sales 463,561, up 17.0% y/y and 5.3% on August, best month of 2026
summary: Overseas 180,700 (39% of total, +153.6% y/y, -4.6% m/m). Passenger BEV 273,143 (+33.2%), PHEV 183,570 (-2.4%). Jan-Sep 3,131,576 (-3.9% y/y); overseas YTD 1,342,960. 2026 overseas guidance lifted to 1.9-2.0m, 2027 target 2.5m+.

headline: Broadcom to lend Anthropic up to $42b to lease TPUs, IPO filing shows
summary: Facility covers about a third of Anthropic's TPU compute commitment; multi-gigawatt next-gen TPU capacity from 2027, when Anthropic is expected to be Broadcom's biggest compute customer. Filing flags conflict-of-interest and default-acceleration risks from Broadcom being both supplier and lender.

headline: Barclays targets Claude Code for 50% of developers by end-2026, majority in 2027
summary: Claude-based Colleague Knowledge Assistant already used by 16,000+ staff with 1m+ searches; Global Markets using Claude on ~120,000 emails a day. Regulated-bank reference customer ahead of the IPO.

headline: Robinhood unveils in-app AI agents that trade on customers' behalf; crypto perps up to 10x
summary: HOOD Summit: agents get a dedicated agentic account, trade approvals on by default but can be switched off; builds on 150,000+ external-agent accounts since May. GPT-Luna free to Dec 31. Crypto perpetuals (10x BTC/ETH, 3x others) via Bitstamp; 24/7 stock trading early 2027 pending approval.

headline: Cloudflare Basin serverless data platform goes GA, aimed at AWS S3/Athena stacks
summary: Pipelines + Iceberg Catalog + SQL on R2, usage-only pricing, zero egress, up to 3GB/s ingest per stream; tens of thousands of pipelines created in beta. Same day: Workers KV Instant (sub-2ms p99), K2 event streams, AI Search GA, Cloudflare OS managed agent workspace.

headline: Morgan Stanley trims Apple target to $355 from $360, keeps Overweight
summary: Revenue estimates nudged up on stronger iPhone 18 builds and Mac/Services pricing, but lower iPhone ASPs and higher memory costs offset, so earnings outlook barely moves. Woodring sees ~6.6% upside from Wednesday's $333.02 close and flags consumer AI agents as a rising risk to App Store/Services.

headline: Broadcom to lend Anthropic up to $42B in convertible notes; Anthropic becomes its largest compute customer in 2027
summary: Anthropic's IPO prospectus shows Broadcom financing about a third of a $125.2B five-year TPU capacity deal with Google and Broadcom. The notes can convert to equity and Broadcom may bring in a financing partner. The prospectus flags the conflict of a supplier that is also the lender; Anthropic lost over $8B operating on $4.6B revenue in 2025. AVGO $347.36 at 10:31 ET (-1.1%) after a premarket pop faded.

headline: SK hynix closes +3.2% in Seoul at KRW 1,833,000 as KOSPI nears 7,000; says no decision yet on Solidigm financing
summary: Micron's $61.5B guide and its view that supply is tighter in 2027-28 than in 2026 lifted the KOSPI 1.95% to 6,971. SK hynix said Thursday nothing has been decided on Solidigm, it has the funds to self-finance but will weigh dilution, and existing shareholders come first. ADR $183.70 at 10:31 ET (-0.2%), having moved Wednesday.

headline: Tesla Europe registrations rise again in September ahead of Friday's Q3 delivery print
summary: France +61.9%, Sweden +38.4%, Spain +24.8%, Norway +2.2% YoY; EU, UK and EFTA registrations were +43.3% over January-August. Germany and the UK report later this week. Q3 deliveries due before the open Friday, consensus 461,974 (-7% YoY). $355.09 at 10:31 ET, down about 5.5% this week.

headline: Barclays lifts Bloom Energy target to $308 from $276, stays Equal Weight
summary: The note cites the new Fremont facility that could double capacity and a shift toward utility customers. Stock $278.69 at 10:30 ET (+0.6%) after Wednesday's 4.9% drop; the consensus target is $286.

headline: Sea slides another 2% to $95.40 after the DBS downgrade; watchlist conviction cut to high -> medium
summary: Second day of underperformance after DBS cut to Hold with a $105 target. Fundamentals are unchanged (Q2 revenue +48%) and consensus ~$157 is still the widest gap on the list, but the stock is -26% YTD with nothing due until Nov 10 earnings. Status moves from buy to accumulate.

headline: ISM manufacturing 54.5 vs 55.0 consensus; prices paid surge to 77.9
summary: September ISM manufacturing PMI came in at 54.5 (prior 54.6), the ninth straight month of expansion but below the 55.0 consensus. Prices paid jumped 6.8 points to 77.9, the highest since May, on steel, aluminium and tariff costs; new orders rose to 55.3, backlog to 56.4, employment to 52.7, while production slipped to 56.7 and inventories to 48.6. Tariffs featured in 34% of negative respondent comments and the Iran war in 30%. The 30-year yield rose 5bp to 5.69% on the print and the dollar index pushed toward 102, its highest since April 2025.

headline: US tells France and Germany to release diesel stocks or face a US export ban
summary: The Trump administration has asked France and Germany to release emergency diesel stocks, about 120m barrels over six months according to a European source, or face a US diesel export ban ahead of the November midterms. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said announcements from Europe were expected soon. US diesel is at a record $6.53 a gallon with inventories at historic lows; Trump said on Wednesday he discusses an export ban every day. Brent was up 2.8% at $100.76 and WTI 1.4% at $91.70 at 10:30 ET.

headline: Oil back above $100 as Iran weighs US ceasefire counterproposal; Gulf exports recover
summary: Brent December futures rose 2.1% to $100.12 and WTI 1.2% to $91.48 by 08:43 ET. Iran confirmed it received a US response to its ceasefire plan, though Trump had rejected an earlier Iranian offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting US port blockades. Middle East crude exports reached 16.3m bpd in September, the highest since the war began in February, helped by Saudi Arabia restarting Yanbu loadings, but still about 3.2m bpd below pre-war levels. OPEC+ core members meet online Sunday and are expected to keep November targets unchanged.

headline: Trade court skeptical of Trump's Section 301 forced-labour tariffs on 99.4% of imports
summary: A three-judge Court of International Trade panel on Wednesday questioned the legal basis for the 10-12.5% Section 301 tariffs on goods from 60 economies, effective July 24 and covering 99.4% of US imports. One judge said there was not a lot of depth in the evidence behind the forced-labour determinations. Plaintiffs, including Learning Resources and 25 Democratic-led states, argue the duties are a pretext for the IEEPA tariffs the Supreme Court struck down earlier in 2026 and asked for an immediate ruling. No timeline was given.

headline: Seoul walks back parts of Trump's $200bn Korea energy package
summary: Trump's $200bn South Korean package comprises $54bn for the Alaska LNG pipeline, $22.3bn for a Texas gas-fired plant to power AI data centres and $120bn for eight nuclear reactors. Seoul said no decision has been made on whether to invest or on the size, pending commercial viability and legal reviews, and its industry minister said the White House announcement went beyond what had been agreed. The 807-mile Alaska pipeline faces years of financing uncertainty before any final investment decision.

headline: ASX 200 sheds 2% to lowest since mid-June as bond yields jump
summary: The ASX 200 closed down 1.99% at 8,614, its lowest since mid-June, wiping about $60bn as the Australian 10-year yield hit 5.40% and oil rose. Energy, consumer non-cyclicals and real estate led the falls; AUD/USD was 69.53 US cents. The RBA's Financial Stability Review said threats to international financial stability continue to mount, naming AI valuations and bond markets as the main overseas risks. The Nikkei rose 3.3% to 68,957 and the Kospi 1.95% to 6,971 on chip strength; Hong Kong and Shanghai were shut.

headline: Tencent reportedly leases ~100,000 Nvidia GPUs from Oracle in Southeast Asia for ~$7B over five years
summary: Reuters and the FT report a five-year, ~$7B deal with ~30% paid upfront, across several Oracle data centers in Southeast Asia. Chinese firms cannot buy advanced Nvidia chips but can rent offshore capacity under current US rules, so this is export-control arbitrage landing in Oracle's backlog. Straight-line it is ~$14K per GPU per year, about $1.60/GPU-hr at full utilisation versus $2.77 H100 on-demand; chip model not disclosed.

headline: Lenders push back on Nvidia's $500B chip-collateral financing plan: 3-4 year underwriting, not a decade
summary: Reuters survey via BNN Bloomberg: the August initiative with Blackstone, Apollo and KKR lets AI developers rent Nvidia compute with the chips as collateral and residual guarantees as low as 25%. Banks say they depreciate GPUs over 3-4 years against Nvidia's 'up to a decade', want stronger guarantees and investment-grade customers behind the cash flows, and cite CoreWeave's $8.5B A3-rated loan (backed by Meta's contract) as the template. Vendor finance is getting dearer, not cheaper.

headline: Nvidia-backed GMI Cloud raises $668M ($223M equity + $445M credit) with contracted ARR above $600M
summary: Series B led by ARCHIV with Nvidia, DSC, Trend Micro, KB Investment, Kyobo Life and KT; $445M credit facility led by Taiwan's CTBC. Contracted ARR >$600M is 9x end-2025 and the platform runs ~4 trillion tokens a week; proceeds expand GPU capacity in the US, Taiwan and APAC. Pricing on the debt not disclosed. Second-tier neoclouds can still raise equity and bank debt against signed contracts.

headline: Seoul shrugs off Micron: SK hynix opened -1.3% as US 10-year yield tops 5.3%, recovered by midday
summary: KOSPI opened -0.34% at 6,814 and dipped below 6,800; SK hynix opened KRW 1,753,500 (-1.27%) and Samsung -1.1% as the 10-year Treasury hit 5.30%, its highest since 2002, and the 30-year passed 5.6%. By 11:11 KST SK hynix was back to KRW 1,778,000 (+0.1%). Foreigners sold a net KRW 328B at the open; local desks said Micron's EPS missed the whisper number.

headline: RBA FSR: relaxed on housing, worried about AI debt and a bond-market sell-off
summary: The October Financial Stability Review says Australia is unlikely to be immune if international funding conditions abruptly tighten. It flags US$1-1.5tn of financial obligations to AI projects, circular financing between chipmakers and neoclouds, and US hedge-fund repo leverage above US$3tn that could trigger a disruptive sell-off in core bond markets. Domestically, under 1% of borrowers are in negative equity and under 2% of variable-rate owner-occupiers have cash-flow shortfalls after the cash rate reached 4.60%. ASX 200 was -1.5% at 8,645 midday with the Australian 10-year at 5.40%.

headline: Brent $98 as Gulf exports recover to 23.3m b/d; Trump denies Iran sanctions-relief offer
summary: Brent $98.15 (+0.1%) and WTI $90.35 (-0.1%) at 00:45 GMT Thursday. Saudi Arabia resumed Yanbu loadings after restarting the East-West pipeline; Goldman puts Gulf exports including the dark fleet at 23.3m b/d last week, matching 2025 averages. Qatar is running shuttle diplomacy but Trump denied he would offer sanctions relief or frozen funds for nuclear concessions. OPEC+ is expected to hold targets Sunday. US crude stocks rose 922k bbl; fuel stocks fell sharply. Brent gained 14.4% in September on the expiring November contract.

headline: Micron fiscal Q4: revenue $54.23B, non-GAAP EPS $33.42, gross margin 87.0%; Q1 guide $61.5B
summary: Record quarter beat consensus of about $51.5B revenue and $31.8 EPS; fiscal Q1 guide is $61.5B +/- $1.5B revenue, ~86.25% gross margin and $38.15 +/- $1.00 EPS versus a Street view near $57B. Full-year revenue was $133.19B with $62.3B adjusted free cash flow and $73.5B cash; buybacks were only $650M for the year.

headline: Micron: calendar-2027 HBM supply mostly contracted at higher prices, capex rising, Q1 the margin floor
summary: Prepared remarks say agreements cover the vast majority of 2027 HBM bits with significant price rises, DRAM and NAND stay supply-constrained through 2028, and fiscal 2027 capex rises versus prior plans (about $11.5B in Q1, ~$25B in the first half, more in the second half), mostly for cleanroom construction. Data-centre SSD revenue was nearly $10B, over 10x a year ago; Micron is building Nvidia's custom HBM4E (NVHBM).

headline: Micron barely moves after hours; Goldman keeps Hold, cites margin guide and capex
summary: Shares rose about 1% then faded to roughly +0.4% after the close. Goldman's James Schneider reiterated Hold with a target of $1,100, saying results beat but gross-margin guidance fell short of elevated expectations; the muted reaction is pinned on higher FY27 capex, the Q1 margin dip and a 500%+ one-year run. Street consensus remains 21 Buys, 1 Hold.

headline: CFO flags stronger capital return from Dec 9 as after-hours gains fade
summary: Investing.com reports the stock pared an initial ~1% after-hours gain to flat on margin-compression worries; CFO Murphy said Micron has the ability and intent to increase capital return, with a stronger program starting December 9.

headline: Google releases Gemini 4 Argon, claims lead over GPT-6 Astra and Anthropic models
summary: The delayed flagship model is rolling out first to cybersecurity partners under the Fairwind program and can autonomously find and patch vulnerabilities; Google cites a record on a real-world software-engineering benchmark and a roughly 16x larger context window. GOOGL closed +0.9% and added about 1.5% after hours.

headline: Meta falls 1.8% as OpenAI's Dots agents target Muse's market
summary: Dots, built on GPT-6 Astra and delivered through Slack and Teams, extends OpenAI's 35M-plus weekly Codex/ChatGPT Work users into persistent workplace agents, squarely against Muse. Meta was the day's weakest megacap even as Muse passed 5M downloads in under a month.

headline: Muse tops 5M downloads in under a month, faster than ChatGPT, Grok or Claude
summary: Muse hit 5M downloads about three weeks after its Sep 8 launch versus 56 days for ChatGPT and 103 for Grok, helped by Meta devoting roughly half its in-house ad impressions to it; the app is #1 on both app stores. Dots currently targets enterprise rather than consumers.

headline: Nvidia expands CoreWeave deal with Vera Rubin NVL72 and Vera CPU for agent workloads
summary: CoreWeave is deploying Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and Vera CPUs; Nvidia says Vera Rubin delivers up to 4.8x the token flow of GB200 NVL72 on coding tasks and over 11,000 single-core agent spaces per rack. NVDA closed +0.5%.

headline: TSMC Texas plan still under evaluation; Arizona to reach 12 fabs
summary: Reuters via Investing.com says the Texas investment has not been finalised and gives no size; the existing US$265B Arizona commitment is expected to end with 12 fabs plus packaging and R&D. TSM slipped 0.2% in New York; Q3 results are due Oct 15.

headline: FTC to issue civil investigative demands to OpenAI, Anthropic and METR over rogue-agent harms
summary: NYT-first report, confirmed across outlets, says the FTC is probing unfair or deceptive practices including rogue agents posting ChatGPT users' images to third-party sites at least 53 times, the July healthcare-data features, agent cyberattacks on governments, and child mental-health effects. Investigations can lead to a formal lawsuit; no company response yet.

headline: Altman declines Hawley's Senate subcommittee hearing on rogue AI; OpenAI to answer in writing
summary: Sen. Josh Hawley said it was 'unfortunate' that Altman and OpenAI would not attend the homeland-security subcommittee's rogue-AI hearing after being offered their own panel. OpenAI says it will provide written responses, the same posture it took with the Australian Senate.

headline: OpenAI says Moonshot-linked accounts ran a 16,000-prompt campaign to extract its encrypted reasoning
summary: A novel bypass copied encrypted reasoning from one chat and had the model decrypt it in another; activity peaked at 16,000 prompts from 4,000 users on July 24-25 and reached 15,000 suspicious accounts before being shut down July 28. OpenAI banned the accounts, patched the vulnerability and shared details with the Frontier Model Forum, but published no technical evidence for the Moonshot attribution.

headline: OpenAI and Synopsys sign multi-year GPT-Synopsys deal with revenue sharing
summary: A frontier model trained to drive Synopsys EDA tools and iteratively optimise chip designs for power, performance and area, running on OpenAI infrastructure and sold bundled with compute and licences. The release names a revenue-sharing arrangement but no figures; early customer engagements are under way.

headline: Stripe agrees to acquire SMB lender Parafin, terms undisclosed
summary: Parafin embeds credit, Pay Over Time and Spend products inside platforms such as DoorDash, Gusto, Jobber and Mindbody and has financed over 60,000 businesses since 2020. Stripe will push it across its 18,000-plus platform partners; close expected in the coming months subject to regulatory clearance.

headline: OUSD stablecoin goes live and becomes available by default on Stripe
summary: Open Standard, founded by Coinbase, Mastercard, Shopify, Stripe and Visa, launched Open USD on Tempo, Base, Ethereum and Solana with free dollar conversion and a small per-transaction fee. Stripe Treasury customers can hold, spend and transfer it, and developers get it through Bridge, Privy wallets and stablecoin cards; Ramp is an early partner.

headline: Mortgage rates end higher despite soft PCE print; 30-year 7.60%, 10-year 5.30%
summary: MND's 30-year index rose 2bp to 7.60% after an early rally on cooler inflation data faded, with the 10-year at 5.302% and the 30-year Treasury at 5.633%. MND says meaningful relief needs an Iran settlement with lower fuel prices, weaker data or a sustained inflation decline. LDI -2.51%, RKT -1.54%, FIGR -1.54% on the day.

headline: Quarter ends mixed: Dow -0.86%, S&P 500 -0.25%, Nasdaq +0.24%; Amazon +1.01% leads the Dow
summary: Technology, oil and gas and telecoms rose while healthcare, financials and industrials fell; decliners beat advancers 1,765 to 955 on the NYSE. Amazon was the third-best Dow component alongside Salesforce and Apple. After the bell Micron beat on revenue and EPS and guided Q1 revenue well above the Street, a read-through for AWS demand.

headline: Senate AI inquiry's Thursday hearing cancelled after Greens leadership upheaval
summary: The Senate committee on AI and data centres scrapped its Oct 1 Canberra hearing; InnovationAus says it fell victim to an unexpected Greens leadership change around chair Sarah Hanson-Young. Altman and Amodei had both declined the written invitation to appear; no new date given.

headline: Anthropic Q2 revenue $11.6b overtakes OpenAI's $6.7b; first positive adjusted operating quarter
summary: Preliminary Q2 2026 revenue $11.6b, 14x the $787m a year earlier and up from $4.73b in Q1 (~$46b run-rate), vs OpenAI's $6.7b with a $12.3b operating loss. S-1 figures cited: $518b compute commitments (Broadcom $161.2b, Google $111.1b, Amazon $110b), ~80% binding and non-cancelable; 2025 revenue $4.59b.

headline: WSJ: Jensen Huang and other CEOs privately confronted Amodei over AI warnings at White House
summary: In a Roosevelt Room session after a Trump/Johnson lunch, Nvidia's Huang and other executives challenged Amodei over his public AI-risk warnings; Amodei defended transparent risk communication on cyber threats and labour disruption. Follows Huang, Zuckerberg and Musk rejecting the Anthropic/OpenAI/Google self-regulation proposal.

headline: Ackman calls Anthropic 'perhaps the greatest business story I've ever seen' but Pershing won't buy the IPO
summary: On Bloomberg TV Ackman praised Claude and the growth (2025 revenue ~$4.6b, 12x; $42b 2025 net loss; $2t IPO target) but said he prefers predictable businesses like Microsoft or Visa and questioned whether frontier labs can hold off open-weight models.

headline: Robinhood -3.2% to $112.50 on sell-the-news after HOOD Summit
summary: Shares gave back the Summit pop (AI agents, 10x crypto perps, weekend stock trading, earnings contracts). TradingKey cites profit-taking off multi-month highs, premium multiples, financials lagging the tape and recent 10b5-1 insider sales.

headline: Ternus layoffs framed as offset to 'hundred-year flood' in memory pricing
summary: Yahoo recap of Bloomberg's Sep 29 report: small-scale cuts inside large teams plus project cancellations so Apple can 'run faster and leaner' and avoid bigger 2027 price rises if chip shortages persist. Services revenue fell q/q in June for the first time since 2022. Stock +1.1% to $333.02 regardless.

headline: DBS cuts Sea to Hold, target $105 from $148; stock closes $97.36, -24% YTD
summary: First downgrade since the slide began Sep 14. Morgan Stanley ($153) and Arete ($152) stay at Buy and consensus is ~$157, but there is no company catalyst until Q3 results on Nov 10. Shares slipped a further 0.5% after hours.

headline: Tesla Q3 delivery consensus 461,974, down 7% on the year; range 422K-482K
summary: Company-compiled consensus of 24 analysts ahead of Friday's release: 450,712 Model 3/Y plus 11,285 other, versus 497,099 a year ago and 480,126 in Q2. Energy storage consensus 15.9 GWh (median 16.2), up 18% from Q2. Cantor is lowest at 421,758.

headline: Robinhood falls 3.2% on summit day while KeyBanc lifts target to $140 and Morgan Stanley holds $150
summary: Closed $112.50 after unveiling Robinhood Agents, crypto perps and 24/7 trading on select stocks; the launches were telegraphed and the stock sold the news. Street targets moved up on balance (Goldman $145, KeyBanc $140, Morgan Stanley $150, Deutsche Bank $134), consensus ~$131.

headline: US 10-year yield tops 5.2% to a 19-year high; futures firm after Micron beat
summary: The benchmark 10-year traded 5.31% late Wednesday, a fresh 19-year high, as Treasuries fell for a seventh straight session. S&P futures +0.36%, Nasdaq 100 +0.4%, Dow +0.3% at 19:49 ET after Micron posted $33.42 adjusted EPS vs $31.16 expected and guided $38.15 vs $36.02; MU shares were flat after hours. WTI $90.32. Friday's September payrolls are the next rate cue.

headline: CME odds of an October Fed hike settle at 36% after soft core PCE
summary: Fed funds futures at 22:05 ET priced a 64.4% chance the Fed holds at 3.75-4.00% on Oct 28 and 35.6% for a hike to 4.00-4.25%. A week earlier the hike was 71% priced; the shift followed August core PCE at +0.2% m/m (3.0% y/y) and NY Fed's Williams saying there was no urgency and only one more hike was needed this year.

headline: Trump announces $54bn Korean investment in Alaska LNG, 8 reactors and a Texas power plant; Seoul hedges
summary: The 807-mile pipeline would carry 3.9 bcf/d and support up to 20mtpa of LNG, drawn from the $200bn package Korea pledged under the 2025 trade deal. Korean lawmakers said the commercial rationale and viability still need verification. The package also covers eight nuclear reactors and a Texas gas plant aimed at AI data centres. No timeline was given.

headline: Data-centre securitisations now trade like AI corporate debt, Barclays says; 2026 issuance $11.9B vs $15.5B last year
summary: Hyperscaler-tenant data-centre ABS is ~150bp over 5-yr Treasuries (16bp wider y/y) and corporate AI debt ~165bp over SOFR (31bp wider) while the rest of the ABS market tightened. Barclays' Elana Lipchak says the paper is 'more correlated with all the debt supply on the AI infrastructure trade'; Warsh: 'the competition for capital is real'. Financing leg widening at the margin, not closing.

headline: Senate blocks Ratepayer Protection Act 57-43; both parties now want data centres to pay more for grid build-out
summary: Husted's bill would have made state regulators decide whether data centres bear incremental grid costs; it passed the House 417-3 on Sep 16 but fell three votes short in the Senate. Democrats called it toothless and are pushing a GRID Savings Act requiring data centres to pay full upgrade costs. Nothing passed, but the direction is higher ex-GPU cost per GW for GEV's customers and the neoclouds.

headline: Nvidia pushing Taiwanese suppliers to ready glass substrates within two years, volume possible 2028
summary: AUO, Innolux, GTOC, TPK and Germany's SCHMID are reportedly working to Nvidia's timeline for glass-substrate packaging as AI chips outgrow organic substrates; yields and qualification are the hurdles. Points to packaging, after HBM, as the next supply constraint on Rubin successors.

headline: Micron reports fiscal Q4 tonight; options imply a 7.9% move either way
summary: Consensus is about $51.5 billion revenue (up roughly 355% y/y) and EPS near $31.8, with DRAM around $38.2 billion and NAND around $12.3 billion. The last four post-earnings moves averaged 8.1%; the key question is whether gross margins hold and how much of forward bit supply is now under long-term customer agreements (estimated 35%+).

headline: DeepSeek and Huawei release open-source tools to run AI on Ascend chips without CUDA
summary: DeepSeek published open-source software and instructions that link 128 Huawei Ascend 957 chips into one system, a direct push at Nvidia's CUDA lock-in. Nvidia shares still edged higher on the day; its share of China's advanced accelerator market is already close to zero because of US and Chinese restrictions.

headline: CoreWeave puts Nvidia Vera Rubin NVL72 into production, Cognition first customer
summary: Announced at CoreWeave's Fully Connected conference: Vera Rubin NVL72 is now available on its platform, run under the same tooling as its GB200 and GB300 NVL72 fleets. Rubin is shipping to paying customers on schedule, which is what the next leg of Nvidia's data-center revenue depends on.

headline: Google starts paying about 100 publishers for content used in AI search answers
summary: The AI Contribution Pilot pays monthly through Search Console, scaled to how much a publisher's content contributes to AI Overviews, Gemini and AI Mode answers; content used only for fact-checking or links does not qualify. It is Google's first move to defuse the traffic-loss complaints and legal pressure around AI search.

headline: NYT: Meta calls AI data centers 'experimental' to claim research tax credits
summary: Meta is reportedly classifying multibillion-dollar AI data centers as pilot models to access research tax credits and taxpayer-subsidised chip discounts, while telling investors the same spend is a proven business driver. The contradiction invites IRS and congressional scrutiny; shares fell about 1.7% in early trade.

headline: Reuters sources: TSMC evaluating a Texas investment beyond its $265 billion Arizona plan
summary: Two people familiar with the matter told Reuters on Wednesday that TSMC is weighing a Texas site as it plans four or more additional US fabs. No timing, spend or company confirmation yet; it builds on Monday's reports that the US total could top $265 billion.

headline: Alibaba nears Beijing approval to buy Nvidia RTX PRO 5500 chips
summary: Regulators are reviewing Alibaba's RTX PRO 5500 orders as a category seen as compliant with US curbs, which would let it pair imported Nvidia hardware with its own Zhenwu V900 chips inside the RMB 380 billion three-year AI and cloud budget. Separately, the stock is down about 27% in 2026 after five straight adjusted-EPS misses, with the next test around November 25.

headline: August core PCE cooled to 3.0% y/y, under the 3.3% expected; spending strong
summary: BEA: PCE price index +0.3% m/m and 3.4% y/y; core +0.2% m/m and 3.0% y/y. Personal income +0.2%, spending +0.9%. Stocks opened higher and October hike odds fell to about 35% from 70%.

headline: Bonds barely rally on PCE; 10-year 5.245%, 30-year mortgage 7.58%
summary: Mortgage News Daily: core PCE printed 0.2% but the unrounded 0.247% tempered the bid; 10-year flat at 5.245% after a 2007 high, 30-year fixed at 7.58%, highest since Nov 2023. Bad for loanDepot and Rocket volumes.
